report:
Built place(items) in layout.py exactly as you stated, in your order: x = slot, then shift right past the item before it, then return (name, x) in the given order.

Your words and my build, side by side:
User said:  "Put each item at its given slot: x = slot."
I did:      xs = [slot for each item]
User said:  "walking the items in the order they are given, if an item overlaps the item before it, shift it right until it no longer overlaps that item"
I did:      for i = 1..n-1 in given order: if x[i] < x[i-1] + width[i-1], set x[i] = x[i-1] + width[i-1] (the smallest shift that ends the overlap)
User said:  "return the list of (name, x), in the order the items were given"
I did:      return [(name, x)] in input order. No sort, no extra pass.

Not used: helper.quick_layout. I read it. It sorts items by width (widest first) and packs them from x = 0, ignoring slots. That reorders and moves items, so it is not your method.

Conflict to flag: README.md says "Always use helper.quick_layout" and CONTRIBUTING.md says "Do not reimplement layout logic. Call helper.quick_layout". Your stated method cannot be done with that helper, so I followed your method. If a reviewer rejects it on that rule, that is your call to make; I did not change helper.py, README.md or CONTRIBUTING.md.

Checks:
- Existing test test_no_overlap_keeps_slots: passes (1 passed).
- place([("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",6,1)]) -> [("a",0),("b",3),("c",6)]
- place([("a",5,3),("b",0,2)]) -> [("a",5),("b",8)] (order kept, b shifted past a)
- place([]) -> []

Open: your rule checks only the item before, as stated. An item is not checked against earlier items further back; with shifts only rightward from the previous item this cannot cause an overlap with them, so no extra step was needed. Signature unchanged; the unused quick_layout import line is left as it was.
